51247632.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to human recombinant N-terminal hexahistidine tagged JAK2 JH1 catalytic domain (835 to 1132 residues) expressed in baculovirus infected Sf9 cells assessed as dissociation constant by surface plasmon resonance assay

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods: The SPR assay was performed on a Biacore T200 instrument (GE Healthcare) at 25 °C. The human recombinant N-terminal hexahistidine tagged JAK2 JH1 catalytic domain (835 to 1132 residues) expressed in baculovirus infected Sf9 cells was immobilized on a CM5 sensor chip via amine coupling. The running buffer was 10 mM HEPES, pH 7.4, 150 mM NaCl, 0.05% P20. The compounds were dissolved in DMSO and diluted with running buffer to the desired concentrations. The association phase was 120 s, and the dissociation phase was 180 s. The regeneration solution was 10 mM glycine-HCl, pH 2.0. The data were analyzed using Biacore T200 evaluation software. The dissociation constant (K_D) was calculated from the binding curves by fitting to a 1:1 Langmuir binding model.
